title: Company All-Hands: Summit Shadow Briefing
summary: All-hands style briefing with Nexera leadership to share Redwood company priorities, roadmap highlights, and operational assurances. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for a regulated workload, security artifacts (SOC2, KMS integration), and a short postmortem from a recent cross-region incident. Customers requested a pilot for Dedicated capacity and a security packet; agreed next steps and owners.
action_items: Maya Chen: Send Dedicated pilot term sheet and seat-based pricing by 2026-06-09
Oren Patel: Share latency/cost benchmark template and recent batch traces by 2026-06-10
Lina Morales: Add Nexera's top 3 prompt sets to evaluation queue and report quality delta by 2026-06-16
Samir Rao: Provide a short summary of the cross-region incident and mitigation timeline by 2026-06-08
Jordan Lee: Confirm internal stakeholders and pilot success criteria by 2026-06-11
next_steps: Schedule Dedicated pilot kickoff (Maya to propose times)
Share security pack (SOC2 report, SSO/SAML guide, KMS integration notes)
Run a quick Dedicated vs Hosted cost/latency benchmark with Nexera's prompts
Arrange engineering deep-dive for infra team if pilot approved
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Oren, Lina, Samir (Redwood); Jordan, Priya, Daniel, Asha, Evan, Kelly (Nexera)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick leadership-level runthrough, no deep demo, focusing on reliability, security, and pilot terms.

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate folks making time this afternoon. This is kind of an all-hands style briefing from our side — quick company priorities, then technical bits, then questions. Jordan, thanks for coordinating.

[00:00:18] Jordan Lee: Yeah thanks Maya, this schedule is perfect. Looking forward, we want to understand risk and cost for moving sensitive PII workloads off-prem.

[00:00:34] Maya Chen: Totally. Quick opener: Redwood has been focusing on three things — predictable inference economics, better reliability across regions, and private deployment controls. We shipped some improvements to routing and cache hit visibility last month.

[00:00:52] Priya Ram: When you say routing improvements, do you mean smarter fallbacks? We saw an outage last quarter that caused long tail latency.

[00:01:05] Oren Patel: Yeah, so the runtime now supports policy-based routing — you can set per-tenant SLOs and the router will prefer lower-latency pools and failover to quantized variants when needed. There was a recent incident, though — quick recap in a bit.

[00:01:22] Daniel Cho: Any chance you can share the postmortem now? The details are important for us.

[00:01:31] Samir Rao: Sure, quick summary: on 2026-05-18 we had a cross-region networking flap that impacted KV cache synchronization, which increased cold-starts and triggered capacity rebalancing. That caused sustained latency spikes in the 99th percentile for about 17 minutes before our fallback policy shifted traffic. We fixed the routing thresholds and added additional health checks.

[00:01:59] Asha Verma: Was that related to the K-V cash — sorry — KV cache replication? The transcript probably said cash earlier, but yeah we need to know if keys were exposed or any logs retained.

[00:02:12] Samir Rao: No PII was exposed. KV cache handles model keys and prefixes, not customer tokens. We also validated S3 and object storage access logs; no unauthorized reads. Postmortem doc will have the timeline and the mitigation steps.

[00:02:30] Maya Chen: We'll share the postmortem snapshot. Oren, can you jump into security integrations?

[00:02:35] Oren Patel: Absolutely. From the compliance angle: we have a SOC2 Type II report available, SSO via SAML or OIDC, RBAC at the route and model level, and KMS integrations — AWS KMS or customer HSM via Bring Your Own Key. For Private deployments we support VPC peering and on-prem bundles.

[00:02:54] Priya Ram: For KMS, do you support key rotation and HSM-backed attestations? We need to show that to our audit team.

[00:03:05] Oren Patel: Yes, automated rotation is supported via AWS KMS policies; for HSMs we have a connector that uses PKCS#11. We'll send the integration guide and a sample attestation flow.

[00:03:19] Evan Moss: On latency/cost tradeoffs — we have a 20ms SLO goal for inference; can Redwood hit that on Hosted? Or do we need Dedicated?

[00:03:30] Lina Morales: It depends on model and prompt lengths. Hosted optimized pools can hit low double-digit ms for smaller models, but for heavy production SLOs with deterministic tail latency, Dedicated pools with pinned instances and KV cache affinity are more reliable. Also, quantization helps reduce cost but may affect quality on some tasks.

[00:03:50] Jordan Lee: That's what we suspected. We want predictable tails — can you demonstrate with our prompts?

[00:03:59] Oren Patel: Yes, we propose a short benchmark: you share the top 3 prompt sets, we'll run both Hosted and Dedicated with identical hardware profiles, and return latency distributions plus token cost.

[00:04:12] Daniel Cho: How long for that?

[00:04:15] Oren Patel: Two to four business days once we have the prompts and a small test dataset. We'll include KV cache-on and cache-off traces to show cold-start impact.

[00:04:28] Kelly Tran: For private deployment, what's the network model? Can we keep traffic inside our VPC?

[00:04:34] Samir Rao: Yes, Private allows customer-managed networking. For cloud Private we do a control plane that talks through a secure channel, but inference traffic and KV caches can be kept in the customer's VPC. On-prem option is fully air-gapped if needed with an ops bundle.

[00:04:50] Asha Verma: Any limitations on model versioning in Private? We want pinning and rollout controls.

[00:04:56] Lina Morales: Same APIs and rollout features exist in Private — canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. The console UI is identical. There may be slight differences in telemetry retention depending on your storage setup but we'll document those.

[00:05:12] Jordan Lee: Pricing — ballpark for Dedicated? We need a monthly guess to size budget.

[00:05:18] Maya Chen: We'll send a Dedicated pilot term sheet. Typical committed pools start at N GPU-months with options for burst, and we can show a model-matching cost estimate. We'll include examples for small-medium-large footprints.

[00:05:30] Priya Ram: Are credits or trial Dedicated options available?

[00:05:33] Maya Chen: For pilots we often provide a time-limited discount and operational support hours. Exact terms on the term sheet.

[00:05:40] Evan Moss: A quick ops question — how do we get visibility into token-level costs? We need to attribute to product teams.

[00:05:46] Lina Morales: The Console gives token- and route-level breakdowns, and there's a token export API. We can also push cost metrics to your Datadog or internal dashboard.

[00:05:56] Daniel Cho: Good. Also, if we go Dedicated, who manages firmware/driver updates on GPUs?

[00:06:02] Samir Rao: For Redwood-hosted Dedicated, we handle driver maintenance in maintenance windows aligned to your SLOs. For Private on-prem, customers can choose to manage or let our team handle via an agent.

[00:06:15] Jordan Lee: Let's talk commitments — our legal team will need the SOC2 and Data Processing Agreement.

[00:06:22] Maya Chen: We'll share the security pack: SOC2 report, DPA template, SSO guide, and our standard SLA. Oren will attach the KMS notes.

[00:06:33] Asha Verma: Please redact any customer-specific data in the SOC2 if needed.

[00:06:36] Maya Chen: Absolutely.

[00:06:40] Jordan Lee: Anything else on the roadmap you want to highlight that might affect us?

[00:06:44] Lina Morales: A couple product notes: in Q3 we're shipping improved prefix caching visibility, better trace linking between tokens and routes, and an optimize feature that suggests quantization profiles per model. Those are relevant if you're trying to compress cost.

[00:07:01] Priya Ram: That optimize tool — can we run it against our test set?

[00:07:05] Lina Morales: Yes, we'll queue Nexera in the evaluation queue after we get the prompts. We'll report quality deltas and suggested quant profiles.

[00:07:14] Jordan Lee: Great. Operationally, our success criteria for a pilot: under 50ms p95 on our main prompt, no PII leakage, and SAML-based SSO integration. If those are met, we proceed to a 6-month commit.

[00:07:30] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll treat that as the working success criteria. Jordan — can you share an internal doc with the pilot stakeholders?

[00:07:36] Jordan Lee: Yes I will.

[00:07:40] Maya Chen: OK, quick recap of owners: I will send pricing and pilot terms, Oren will send benchmarks and security pack, Lina will run evals on your prompts, Samir will share the incident postmortem. Any final questions?

[00:07:58] Evan Moss: One ask — can Redwood provide a short RTO/RPO statement for the Dedicated pools? We need it for our SRE runbook.

[00:08:06] Samir Rao: Yes, we'll include an RTO/RPO section in the postmortem/ops doc.

[00:08:12] Kelly Tran: Thanks everyone, that's helpful.

[00:08:16] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up over email with attachments and proposed times. Appreciate the time.

[00:08:24] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript has small ASR artifacts — e.g., K-V cash, some names spelt phonetically. The call behaved like a leadership update with technical breakouts but did not include a product demo.
